children: Hudson River Trading, a major Wall Street market maker, generated $21.4B of revenue in the first nine months of 2026, already eclipsing its full-year record of $12.3B set in 2025, according to a media report on Wednesday.

The company that uses technology and quantitative analysis to match buyers and sellers across asset classes posted $3.6B of trading revenue in Q3, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter. That's down slightly from the same quarter a year ago.

HRT's Q3 EBITDA came to ~$2.4B, while net income was little changed from a year ago at $2.2B, the people said. The company disclosed the most recent quarter's performance to its debt holders on Tuesday. Its executives told them the company plans to continue to increase spending on trading infrastructure, including data centers and access to compute power, the people said.
Volatility on Wall Street during the third quarter pressured earnings at some trading desks after a record first half for many trading companies, including HRT and its rivals.

Citadel Securities, a key competitor, produced more than $3.4B of revenue in Q3 and more than $15B of net trading revenue for the first nine months of 2026. That also topped its full-year 2025 record, Bloomberg said, citing a person with knowledge of the matter.
